title.value: Model description paper Development and evaluation of the Aerosol Forecast Member in the National Center for Environment Prediction (NCEP)'s Global Ensemble Forecast System (GEFS-Aerosols v1)

scope_reason: Although a forecast-model description paper, it evaluates forecasts of smoke aerosol from wildfire/biomass-burning events (Amazon and southern Africa, 2019) and of dust events against observations.

scope_quote.evidence_text: To validate model performance when using the GBBEPx v3 fire emissions with a plume rise module based on realtime FRP data, we compare the real-time GEFS-Aerosols AOD with other reanalysis data, satellite observations, and the NGACv2 model for the big fire event in August 2019.

evidence.evidence_text: At the Alta Floresta site, which is in the middle of the Amazon fire source region, the daily AOD variations of both the ICAP and GEFS-Aerosols Day-1 predictions are quite consistent with those of the AERONET data, especially as they are able to reproduce two peaks in AOD enhancements in late August and late September caused by fire plumes (Fig. 9a). The correlation (RMSE) is 0.66 (0.23), 0.9 (0.12), and 0.68 (0.31) for GEFS-Aerosols, ICAP, and NGACv2.
